sources.whitecapCoefficient: Whitecap coverage W = 3.84e-6 U^3.41 (Monahan & O'Muircheartaigh 1980), taken as the share of waves that break
sources.breakingDepthRatio: A wave breaks in water shallower than 1.28 times its height (McCowan 1894)
sources.breakingSteepness: A wave breaks once it is as steep as a wave can stand, a seventh as high as it is long (Michell 1893): a breaker is as long as its height makes it, and runs at that length's speed, no faster than the sea's own waves
sources.plungingShareAtSea: In deep water about 2% of breaking waves plunge, entraining air deep; the rest spill (Gemmrich & Farmer 1999, Journal of Physical Oceanography 29(10), 'Observations of the scale and occurrence of breaking surface waves')
sources.plungingIribarren: On a sloping bed a wave plunges when tan(slope) / sqrt(H / L0) lies between 0.5 and 3.3; below it spills, above it surges (Battjes 1974)
sources.plungeDistance: A plunging crest lands H (4.0 - 9.25 m) shoreward of where it breaks, on a bed of slope m (Galvin 1969, 'Breaker travel and choice of design wave height'); shoreward of that, what reaches a hull is the broken wave's bore
sources.bedSlopeBlocks: The bed's slope is read over this many blocks to seaward, across the surf zone, where whole blocks of depth still give it to a sixteenth
sources.slamCoefficient: A plunging crest strikes a flat panel with a space-averaged pressure 1/2 rho C v^2, C not less than 2 pi with cushioning and three-dimensional effects (DNV-RP-C205, 2010, 8.7.2.5); a spilling crest's roller presses only its stagnation pressure, 1/2 rho c^2
sources.plungingSpeedRatio: A plunging breaker strikes at 1.2 times its phase velocity (DNV-RP-C205, 2010, 8.8.1.2); its phase velocity follows the period and the depth (Eckart 1952)
sources.shippedWaterFraction: Balance: the share of a crest's water that stays aboard once it comes over the gunwale
sources.crestRatio: A linear wave's crest stands half its height above still water
sources.breakingCrestRatio: A breaking crest is peaked: Stokes' highest wave stands about 0.6 of its height above still water, a plunging breaker 0.7 to 0.8
sources.waveDriftCoefficient: Mean wave drift force is rho g H^2 / 16 per metre of beam on a body that reflects every wave; a small craft, short against the wavelength, reflects about a tenth

sources.rainMillimetresPerHour: Heavy rain is about 10 mm an hour; it falls at full rainfall, per game hour

sources.capsizes: Off until a capsized vessel is seen to roll over (#100); swamping and breaker strikes stay on
sources.speedExponent: At the same paddling power P = D v, with drag D growing with wetted area, which grows as displacement to the 2/3, and with v squared: v goes as displacement to the -2/9
sources.freeSurfaceRoll: Balance: water sloshing across the bilge leans with every roll and adds to it; a full bilge doubles it
sources.freeSurfaceCapsize: Balance: the free surface takes away stability, so a full bilge goes over to a breaker half as high

sources.heaveAddedMass: A hull heaving drags about its own mass of water with it: heave period 2π √((M + A₃₃) / (ρ g A_w)), with A₃₃ about M for a small open boat (Aalto seakeeping notes, SD06)
sources.heaveDamping: Balance: a boat that rises to a crest settles in a bob or two, radiating waves as it goes
sources.rollDamping: A small hull without bilge keels rolls on for several swings: damping ratio about 0.06 to 0.1 (boatdesign.net, a 25 m patrol boat)

sources.anchoredExposure: Balance: an anchored vessel takes three tenths of the pull of wind and waves and the shipped water an unanchored one does; it lies across the sea, so it capsizes as if beam-on
sources.anchorFullScope: Seamanship: a rode of 5 to 7 times the depth holds fully

sources.hazardPerSquareMetreHour: Balance: how likely each game hour of waves this high is to throw a moored vessel on the shore it swings against
sources.surfReachPerMetre: Balance: how far beyond its swing, per metre of wave height, the surf still reaches a moored vessel
sources.shoreSearchBlocks: The farthest the shore is looked for, past the swing and the surf: more than the longest swing, an anchor's 210 m of rode
sources.coarseSearchStride: Past fineSearchBlocks the shore is looked for every few blocks: land that far is coastline, and unloaded ground is read from the ocean map, which is coarser still

sources.tallestMastMetres: The farthest a strike is searched for a mast to draw it: as tall as the tallest vessel's mast
sources.attractBlocksPerMastMetre: A mast protects, and draws strikes from, a cone of about its own height in radius

sources.trains: Wave trains spread around the wind, longest first; their energies sum to the sea's, so the significant height drawn is the sea state's
sources.lengthFactor: The peak wave's length follows its period by deep-water dispersion, L = g T^2 / 2 pi
sources.minLengthBlocks: The water mesh has one vertex a block: shorter waves alias
sources.surfFoam: Off until the surf foam reads white over any seabed (#70); the foam offshore stays on
sources.caps: The share of the sea's area under whitecaps: above Monahan's measured coverage (3.84e-6 U^3.41), so the caps read from afar as the descriptions have them
sources.whitecaps: The Beaufort scale's sea descriptions: scattered whitecaps at 3, frequent at 4 and many at 5, foam blown in streaks along the wind from 6 and well marked at 7 to 8, spray and a sea turning white from 8 up
